one_month_reasoning: Lumentum's own fiscal Q1 FY27 report is expected around 2026-11-03 (third-party calendar), i.e. just after the 2026-11-01 target date (a Sunday, so the effective print is the 2026-10-30 close). So the company's own print is most likely outside the window. Inside the window: the late-October hyperscaler earnings (Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon), whose capex guidance moves the AI-optics group sharply in both directions, plus pre-earnings positioning and peer read-throughs. The stock just ran from about $921 to $1085 in a week and sits at a 52-week high. Meanwhile insiders are selling steadily: the CFO sold 24.5k shares at about $1048 on 2026-10-01, and the president files near-daily Form 144s. That argues for a slight mean-reversion tilt, but momentum and a guide that beat consensus argue the other way. Net: an almost symmetric lognormal at about 26% monthly vol (97% annual / 3.5, slightly shrunk), with the median a touch below spot (about $1083 before the vol-drag adjustment).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS $32 x 30x + $11/sh net cash = $971, weight 0.6), EV/sales (FY28 revenue $7.5B x 12x + net cash = $885, weight 0.25) and a cycle-normalized P/E ($32 x 20x + net cash = $651, weight 0.15), giving about $900 on about 103M fully diluted shares.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Jul-2027 to Jun-2028, roughly the NTM window at the horizon) non-GAAP EPS $32 x 30x = $960, plus net cash $11/sh

inputs_detail.derivation: Street FY28 range runs from >$30 (TD Cowen) to $38.95 (BNP). The Q1 FY27 guide of $4.05-4.35 annualizes to about $17, and continued sequential growth plus a 100-200bp operating-margin lift implies $30+. I take the low end ($32) because of the supply-normalization and pricing-reset risk (sources 6, 10).

The stock traded at about 55x forward in June 2026 (source 6) and about 47x NTM now (1085 / ~$23). As growth decelerates from about 100% toward 30-40% by late 2027, I assume compression toward about 30x, still a premium to historical optical-component multiples.
Cash and short-term investments of $2.7B (source 1) less $1.545B of convertible-note principal, which must be settled in cash (source 2), is about $1.16B. Divided by 103M diluted shares, about $11.

89.7M common (10-K cover) + 2.9M NVIDIA convertible preferred + about 8M net shares from in-the-money converts (2032 notes at $187.77, 2029 at $69.54, 2028 at $131.03, 2026 at $99.29; principal settled in cash) + about 2.5-3M awards (source 1 cites 3.1M).

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue $7.5B x 12x EV/sales = $90B EV / 103M shares + $11 net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: The Q1 FY27 guide of $1.25B mid-point grows about 7-8% sequentially, giving FY27 about $5.6B; pump-laser shipments are to rise 4x over several quarters but are capacity-capped (source 8), so FY28 grows about 33% to about $7.5B.

A 40% non-GAAP operating margin (Q1 guide 39.5-40.5%, source 1) with about 15% tax gives about 34% net margin, and 12x sales is about 35x earnings. That is set slightly below the P/E method to reflect cyclicality.

inputs_detail.derivation: This captures the skeptic case that the industry reverts to normal multiples once EML/pump-laser shortages ease. Source 6 flags the pricing reset once supply catches up; sources 13 and 14 show the group de-rating sharply on sentiment shifts and downgrades.

bear.story: The AI-capex digestion and supply-catch-up scenario. Chinese InP/EML entrants (Yuanjie's 200G EML in mass production around end-2026) and Broadcom/Coherent capacity close the >30% shortage. 200G EML pricing (about $10-12, >90% GM) resets, Customer A (26.6% of FY26 revenue) digests inventory, and CPO slips. FY28 EPS of about $22 x 22x.

base.story: Execution continues and FY27 EPS is about $19-20. By late 2027 the market capitalizes FY28 EPS of about $32 at about 30x as growth slows from 100% toward 30-40%. That is roughly flat to slightly down from $1085 after a +533% year.

bull.story: Shortages persist through 2028. CPO/NPO and external-light-source orders pull forward, and OFC 2027 targets are raised (the operating-margin target is already hinted +100-200bp). FY28 EPS of $40+ at about 40x.

thesis_break_reason: Around $640 (-41%) the stock would sit below the spring 2026 pullback lows (the CFO sold near $691 earlier in 2026) and below a 20x multiple on $32 FY28 EPS. Trading there would most likely mean the FY28 earnings power itself was being cut: an EML/pump pricing reset from Chinese capacity, a Customer A order cut, or a hyperscaler capex reduction. Multiple compression alone would not get there.

reasoning: Basic facts come from the company's filings. Q4 FY26 revenue was $1.01B (+109%), non-GAAP EPS $3.23, and the Q1 FY27 guide is $1.25B / $4.05-4.35 at about a 40% operating margin. Cash is $2.7B, including the $2B NVIDIA preferred, against $1.545B of converts. Diluted shares are about 103M. Skeptic-lane evidence: (1) concentration, with Customer A at 26.6% of revenue, up from 15.4%; (2) earnings quality, since FY26 FCF was only about $300M (OCF $751M - capex $451M) and GAAP showed a $7.8B extinguishment loss from equitizing converts, so share dilution has been large; (3) insiders are selling steadily into strength under 10b5-1 plans, with about $59.5M in 90 days, the CFO selling 24.5k shares at $1048 on 10/1 (about 25% of his holding) and the president filing near-daily Form 144s; (4) competition, as Chinese InP makers such as Yuanjie expect 200G EML mass production by end-2026 into a market where Lumentum earns >90% GM at about $10-12/unit; management denies near-term impact; (5) history of violent drawdowns (-20% in June, -9% in a May photonics reset, earlier downgrades) and bears' 'priced for perfection' framing at 55x forward. I weighed these honestly against a strong, sold-out order book and Street FY28 EPS of $30-39. The result: FY28 EPS of about $32 at a compressed 30x, blended with EV/sales and a cycle-normalized method, gives fair value of about $900, below the $1085 spot. Scenarios at 25/50/25 ($500 / $1000 / $1700) give a mean of about $1050 and a median of about $1000. The ladder is a lognormal with median about $1000 and sigma about 0.65, below the trailing 97% realized vol because some of that was a one-off re-rating. That puts P(>=spot) at 0.45, slightly bearish but not a confident call; the right tail is kept fat because AI-optics upside surprises have repeatedly happened.
